To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the full spectrum inversion technique is capable of reconstruct the fine vertical structure in the lower tropospheric atmosphere in the presence multipath.

the full-spectrum-inversion technique is successfully adapted to retrieve atmospheric properties from simulated airborne GPS radio signals, which is a necessary step toward the use of the technique for real data analysis.

(1) the full-spectrum inversion (FSI) technique is successfully applied to simulated airborne GPS radio occultation (AROGO) signals, and (2) the FSI-retrievals are capable of reconstructing atmospheric properties in the lower tropopause, where the GO method is challenged by strong signal multipath.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the application of the full-spectrum radio occultation (RO) inversion algorithm to simulated ARO signals.
a new technique to reconstruct the atmospheric refractivity and bending angle profile from GPS signals measured by airborne GPS receivers, which is based on the FSI technique.

the retrieval of atmospheric properties (bent angle and refractivity) using the full-spectrum-inversion (FSI) technique applied to simulated GPS radio-occultation (RO) signals from an airborne GPS receiver.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ARO GPS RO technique is capable of providing high-resolution, high-accuracy bending angle and refractive index profiles in the lower tropospheric region, where the GO method fails.
the FSI algorithm is capable of retrieving atmospheric properties (bent path and refractivity) in the presence of strong multipath in the ARO case, which otherwise leads the GO algorithm to fail.
the FSI method has been successfully adapted and demonstrated for ARO data.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the FSI algorithm can be applied to the ARO signal, and it has the potential to retrieve the bending angle and refractivities from the surface up through the tropopause.
we developed an end-to-end ARO FSIR simulation system to study the ARO GPS RO technique and its performance, which is a necessary step for the future development of the ARO RO technique.
the ARO FSI technique can retrieve the bending angle and refractive index profiles with high vertical resolution, which is a key advantage over the GO technique.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the ARO GPS RO technique has a great potential for improving our understanding of the fine vertical structure in the lower tropospheric atmosphere, which is of great importance to weather forecasting and numerical weather prediction.
the FSI is an attractive technique for retrieving atmospheric properties from ARO signals.
the FSI algorithm is a promising approach for the retrieval of ARO bending angles and refractivity, which can be used for atmospheric sounding, weather forecasting, and ionosphere studies.
